findings.issue: /readiness renders 37.6 KB of markdown (193 rows) as 750 KB of HTML with 3,240 elements, because every row repeats long utility-class strings in both the HTML and the duplicate RSC payload. Seven class strings account for about 278 KB (37%) of the page.
findings.impact: Transfer is fine at 46 KB gzip, but the server streams and gzips 750 KB per request, so the prerendered /readiness served 151 req/s against 1,562 req/s for /skills on the same server (local M1 Pro production build, not Fly shared-cpu-1x hardware); on a shared-cpu-1x the ratio holds at far lower absolute numbers. On a low-end phone the browser parses 750 KB of HTML plus RSC payload and hydrates about 3,240 elements, more than double the size Lighthouse flags as an excessive DOM. /example/foundry-2026-10-07 has the same shape at 505 KB.
findings.evidence: components/ReadinessMap.tsx:98-103: `<div className="flex gap-x-4 sm:block">` / `<dt className="w-[6.5rem] shrink-0 font-mono text-[0.6875rem] leading-5 text-bone-faint sm:mb-0.5 sm:w-auto lg:sr-only">` / `<dd className="min-w-0 text-sm leading-5 text-bone-dim [overflow-wrap:anywhere]">`, rendered three times per row (Field for Owner, Applies when, Evidence at lines 119-129) across 193 rows; components/ReadinessMap.tsx:113 `className={`grid scroll-mt-28 gap-x-6 gap-y-3 py-4 lg:items-baseline ${LG_COLUMNS}`}` per row. Measured on the served page: the dt class string occurs 1,158 times (579 in HTML, 579 in the RSC payload) = 119,274 B; the dd class 1,158 times = 74,112 B; top seven strings 278,398 B of 750,384 B. The RSC payload (`self.__next_f.push`) is 448,985 B, 59.8% of the document, and repeats every className (3,143 occurrences). Element count in the HTML body: 3,240. HTML raw 750,392 B, gzip 45,795 B. autocannon -c 10: /readiness 151 req/s gzip (184 identity), /skills 1,562 req/s gzip (2,050 identity).
findings.recommendedFix: Hoist the per-row class lists into a few named component classes in globals.css (for example `.rm-field`, `.rm-label`, `.rm-value` via @apply, or parent-scoped `[&_dt]:` variants on the `<ul>`), so each row carries a short class or none. That shrinks both the HTML and the RSC copy. If the page keeps growing, collapse each area behind a `<details>` or render the area list with per-area anchors only above the fold. Declare a client budget (see notAssessed) so the next growth is judged against a number.
findings.reproduction: curl -s -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' -w '%{size_download}' -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3107/readiness (45,795) and without the header (750,392); count `w-[6.5rem] shrink-0` occurrences in the raw body (1,158); npx autocannon@7.15.0 -c 10 -d 8 -H 'Accept-Encoding=gzip' against /readiness and /skills.

findings.issue: /skills/[slug] and /example/[slug] render on every request although their inputs are fixed files baked into the image: neither exports generateStaticParams, so the build prerenders neither and each hit re-reads and re-renders.
findings.impact: The shared self-audit URL is the heaviest page that renders per request: 67 req/s, p50 141 ms, p99 261 ms locally with 10 connections, and /skills/production-audit 57 req/s, p99 274 ms (local M1 Pro production build, not Fly shared-cpu-1x hardware). A link spike to the public example lands on the slowest path of a single shared-cpu-1x machine, where these figures fall by an order of magnitude. Nothing breaks at today's traffic.
findings.evidence: app/example/[slug]/page.tsx:25-31: `export default async function ExampleReport({` ... `const report = getPublicReport(slug);` with no `generateStaticParams` export in the file; app/skills/[slug]/page.tsx:25-31 `export default async function SkillPage({` ... `const skill = getSkill(slug);`, same absence (grep for generateStaticParams over app/ returns nothing). `.next/prerender-manifest.json` routes: `/`, `/behind`, `/behind/brand`, `/behind/design-system`, `/behind/product`, `/readiness`, `/skills` and no dynamic routes. Served headers: /example/foundry-2026-10-07 and /skills/production-audit return `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` with no `x-nextjs-prerender`, while /skills returns `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`. Note: TODOS.md:49 still says `13 content routes uncached SSR`; at HEAD the uncached content routes are these two (plus /reports and /unlock, which must be dynamic).
findings.recommendedFix: Export `generateStaticParams` from both pages (skill slugs from listSkills(), public report slugs from listPublicReports()) with `dynamicParams = false` or a notFound fallback, so the routes prerender at build like /skills. The inputs only change with a deploy, so no revalidation is needed. Update the TODOS.md:49 count in the same change.

findings.issue: The site scales to zero, so the first request after idle pays a machine start plus Node boot, recorded at about 8 s, against the version check's 10 s client timeout and the first human visitor's patience.
findings.impact: On a low-traffic public site many sessions start cold, so the first visitor after idle waits several seconds for the marketing page. An adopter whose daily version check lands on a cold start slower than 10 s gets no upgrade notice that day: the one-liner writes the stamp even after curl fails (`;` before `touch`), so the retry waits 24 hours. Nothing hangs; the timeout and `|| true` hold.
findings.evidence: fly.toml:33-35: `auto_stop_machines = "stop"` / `auto_start_machines = true` / `min_machines_running = 0`; fly.toml:46-47 `size = "shared-cpu-1x"` / `memory = "512mb"`. skills/production-audit/SKILL.md:172 (same block in all 11 skills): `curl -m 10 -fsS "https://foundry.thehorizonfoundry.com/api/version?skill=production-audit&v=0.2.1"; touch "$HOME/.claude/.foundry-version-checked" 2>/dev/null; } || true`. NOTES.md:334 `10s timeout for measured ~8s cold starts`.
findings.recommendedFix: Measure the cold start on Fly (see notAssessed). If it is near 8 s, either set `min_machines_running = 1` (one shared-cpu-1x is a few dollars a month) or switch `auto_stop_machines` to `suspend`, which resumes from a memory snapshot in well under a second. Touch the stamp only on success, or retry once, so a cold-start timeout does not cost the adopter a day.
findings.assumption: The cold start is about 8 s as NOTES.md:334 records; this run could not stop or start a Fly machine to measure it.

findings.issue: posthog-js is imported at module scope, so about 72 KB gzip (221 KB raw) of its 250 KB gzip shared JavaScript ships on every route, even in builds with no key; prerendered routes also preload 8 font files (126 KB), including weights a route may not use.
findings.impact: Every visitor on a low-end phone downloads and parses roughly 29% more JavaScript than the site's own code needs before analytics has anything to send. No budget is declared, so the site cannot say whether it passes. Tracked already at TODOS.md:228 and TODOS.md:230.
findings.evidence: instrumentation-client.ts:1 `import posthog from "posthog-js";` with the init guarded later at :10 `if (key) {`. Served chunk `/_next/static/chunks/3118i1wxv842-.js` is 220,846 B raw, 71,738 B served gzip, and contains the posthog-js runtime (`posthog.capture`, `rrweb`, surveys code); it is referenced by every measured route although this build inlines no PostHog browser key. Shared JS per route sums to 249,833 to 252,431 B gzip. Font preloads: 8 `<link rel="preload" ... as="font">` on /, /readiness (126,288 B total); lib/fonts.ts:36-52 loads Plex Sans in 4 weights, Plex Mono in 3 and Plex Serif in 3.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the import inside the key guard as a dynamic `import("posthog-js")` (or initialize on requestIdleCallback) so the library leaves the initial graph, per the existing TODOS.md:228 entry. Set `preload: false` on font families or weights not used above the fold. Declare a per-route JS budget in DESIGN.md so this is judged rather than described.
